title: Magnetic catalysis and Hall conductivity of excitonic insulators in a planar four-Fermi model
authors: William R. Tavares, Rudnei O. Ramos, Nei Lopes
abstract: We study the effects of a perpendicular magnetic field on the excitonic insulator (EI) phase in the semiconductor regime using an extended planar four-Fermi model. Within the large-$N$ approximation, we determine the coupled scalar and excitonic condensates at finite temperature, chemical potential, and magnetic field. The field enhances the EI condensate and raises its critical temperature, providing an excitonic realization of magnetic catalysis, while the scalar condensate remains constant throughout the EI phase. By contrast, the critical chemical potential depends nonmonotonically on the field because of the successive occupation of Landau levels. The magnetic field also shifts the mean-field tricritical point and enlarges the first-order region of the temperature--chemical-potential phase diagram. We further analyze the Hall conductivity and find that increasing the field reduces the number of plateaus and modifies the threshold for a finite Hall response. For the parameters considered, the emergence of the EI condensate is accompanied by a characteristic change in the Hall conductivity, including a field-dependent change of slope near a continuous transition. These results show that the combined phase structure and Hall response can provide complementary signatures of excitonic ordering in planar fermionic systems.
summary: This paper theoretically examines the effect of a magnetic field on an excitonic insulator phase using a four-Fermi model. It finds that the magnetic field enhances the excitonic order parameter, demonstrating a form of magnetic catalysis. Furthermore, it predicts characteristic changes in the Hall conductivity that serve as complementary signatures for detecting this type of electronic ordering.
main_problem: The study investigates how a perpendicular magnetic field affects the excitonic insulator (EI) phase and its associated Hall conductivity in planar fermionic systems.
main_result: The magnetic field induces an 'excitonic realization of magnetic catalysis' by enhancing the EI condensate, while the Hall conductivity exhibits characteristic changes accompanying this ordering transition.
method: The analysis employs the large-$N$ approximation within a mean-field framework to derive and minimize the thermodynamic potential for coupled scalar and excitonic condensates.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using an extended planar four-Fermi model (extended Gross-Neveu model) describing electron-hole coherence interactions in the semiconductor regime. The Hamiltonian incorporates minimal coupling to a perpendicular magnetic field.
key_observables: EI condensate ($\eta_c$), critical temperature ($T_c$), Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}$), and phase structure changes (e.g., tricritical point).
important_parameters: Perpendicular magnetic field ($B$), finite temperature ($T$), and chemical potential ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-$N$ approximation and treats the system using a homogeneous saddle-point mean-field approach, neglecting collective phase fluctuations.
figures_summary: Not specified by notes; the text describes analyzing field dependence of condensates and Hall conductivity near transitions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the model (Section II), derives the thermodynamic potential in zero field, establishes gap equations for equilibrium condensates, and then extends this framework to incorporate a perpendicular magnetic field (Section III).
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter theory, the study of emergent collective phases like excitonic insulators under external fields provides insights into many-body ground states that are relevant to strongly correlated systems.
